_about: Money Quest quote series. `verification` must be "verified" before a video can be produced. 12 of the 15 quotations were checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text of the original work; Dewey (1897), Clear and Kahneman were confirmed from transcriptions or the author's own published text. Never change `quote` without re-verifying. `rights` records why the quotation may be used. No quoted author endorses Money Quest.

quotes.pillar: Financial literacy and healthy money habits
quotes.hook: Where does your child's pocket money go?
quotes.quote: Beware of little expenses; a small leak will sink a great ship.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: Benjamin Franklin, "The Way to Wealth" (Father Abraham's speech, preface to Poor Richard Improved, 1758).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #20203) on 16 November 2026. Spelling modernised from "Expences"; capitalisation normalised.
quotes.takeaway: Small spending choices add up. Children can learn to notice them.
quotes.cta: Try the spending activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Franklin wrote this in 1758, and it still fits a child's pocket money. Small, everyday spending choices are where money habits begin. Noticing them is a skill children can practise.

quotes.hook: Does your child give up when things get hard?
quotes.quote: I'm not afraid of storms, for I'm learning how to sail my ship.
quotes.author: Louisa May Alcott
quotes.source: Louisa May Alcott, Little Women, Part Second (1869), chapter 44. Spoken by the character Amy.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #514) on 16 November 2026. Spoken by the character Amy in chapter 44.
quotes.takeaway: Resilience grows through practice, not perfection.
quotes.cta: Try the Emotion Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Amy says this near the end of Little Women. Resilience isn't the absence of difficulty. It's the growing sense that you can handle it, and children build that sense through small, safe practice.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.hook: How do children really learn about money?
quotes.quote: Education … is a process of living and not a preparation for future living.
quotes.author: John Dewey
quotes.source: John Dewey, "My Pedagogic Creed", The School Journal, vol. 54 (16 January 1897), Article I. Full sentence: "I believe that education, therefore, is a process of living and not a preparation for future living."
quotes.verification_note: Confirmed in multiple transcriptions of the 1897 text. The ellipsis marks the omitted word "therefore". The popular version "Education is life itself" is a paraphrase and is not used.
quotes.takeaway: Children learn by doing, one real choice at a time.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Dewey's point from 1897: learning isn't a rehearsal for later. Children learn when they take part in real things now, like choosing, planning and trying, with support.

quotes.hook: How do you raise a responsible child?
quotes.quote: Few things help an individual more than to place responsibility upon him, and to let him know that you trust him.
quotes.author: Booker T. Washington
quotes.source: Booker T. Washington, Up from Slavery: An Autobiography (1901), chapter XI.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #2376) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Trust and small responsibilities help children grow.
quotes.cta: Try Leadership Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Washington wrote this about running a school, and it holds for a family too. A small, real responsibility, given with trust, is one of the simplest ways to help a child grow.

quotes.hook: Why does that toy feel so urgent right now?
quotes.quote: Nothing in life is as important as you think it is, while you are thinking about it.
quotes.author: Daniel Kahneman
quotes.source: Daniel Kahneman, "Focusing Illusion", Edge.org annual question essay (2011); the idea is developed in Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011), chapter 38.
quotes.verification_note: Wording confirmed from Kahneman's own Edge essay. The book's chapter 38 wording should be checked if the book is cited alone.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.takeaway: A short pause helps children choose with care.
quotes.cta: Try the Brain Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: In the moment, the thing a child wants can feel like the only thing that matters. Adults feel it too. A short pause before deciding is a habit worth practising together.

quotes.hook: Is your child afraid of getting it wrong?
quotes.quote: We often discover what will do, by finding out what will not do; and probably he who never made a mistake never made a discovery.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Samuel Smiles, Self-Help; with Illustrations of Conduct and Perseverance (1859), chapter XI.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #935) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Testing an idea, and learning from it, is how children create.
quotes.cta: Try Entrepreneur Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Every young inventor needs to hear this. An idea that doesn't work is information, not failure. Children learn to create by testing small ideas and trying again.

quotes.hook: Why do small things feel so big to children?
quotes.quote: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: Epictetus, The Encheiridion, section V, translated by George Long (1877).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #10661) on 16 November 2026. The sentence continues with an example, omitted here.
quotes.takeaway: Children can learn to notice a feeling before they act.
quotes.cta: Try the Emotion Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: An idea almost two thousand years old: what we tell ourselves about an event shapes how it feels. Children can learn to notice a feeling and choose a next step.

quotes.hook: What does that toy really cost your child?
quotes.quote: The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #205) on 16 November 2026. The sentence begins mid-clause in the original; the first letter is capitalised.
quotes.takeaway: Children can learn to ask what a purchase really costs.
quotes.cta: Try the budgeting activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Thoreau measured cost in life, not money: the time and effort something takes to earn. It's a useful question for a child weighing a purchase against a savings goal.

quotes.hook: What is the one skill your child will always need?
quotes.quote: The object and reward of learning is continued capacity for growth.
quotes.author: John Dewey
quotes.source: John Dewey, Democracy and Education (1916), chapter eight, "Aims in Education".
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #852) on 16 November 2026. The clause follows "or that" in the original; the first letter is capitalised.
quotes.takeaway: Learning how to keep learning is a skill for life.
quotes.cta: Try the Future Skills activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: For Dewey, the point of learning was the ability to keep learning. That matters even more for children growing up with tools that change every year.

quotes.pillar: Financial literacy and healthy money habits
quotes.hook: Can one coin a week change a habit?
quotes.quote: Every action you take is a vote for the type of person you wish to become.
quotes.author: James Clear
quotes.verification_note: Confirmed on the author's own site, which publishes the chapter 2 excerpt and repeats the sentence.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.cta: Try the saving activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: A coin in a jar is a small thing. Repeated every week, it becomes evidence a child can point to: "I'm someone who saves."

quotes.hook: Can small savings really reach a big goal?
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: Benjamin Franklin, "The Way to Wealth" (1758), quoting his earlier Poor Richard's Almanack.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #20203) on 16 November 2026. Capitalisation normalised.
quotes.takeaway: Small savings, repeated, reach big goals.
quotes.cta: Set a savings goal on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: One small step doesn't look like much. Franklin's point is that many of them do the work. A savings goal lets a child see that for themselves.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.hook: Why do early habits matter so much?
quotes.quote: The great thing in all education is to make our nervous system our ally instead of our enemy.
quotes.author: William James
quotes.source: William James, Talks to Teachers on Psychology (1899), chapter VIII, "The Laws of Habit".
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #16287) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Good habits, started early, make later choices easier.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: William James argued that habits do much of the work for us, for better or worse. Small routines practised in childhood, like saving a coin or checking a list, become things a child no longer has to think about.

quotes.hook: How do children learn to trust themselves?
quotes.quote: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #2944) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Confidence grows when children make real choices.
quotes.cta: Try the Money Simulator on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Self-trust isn't something we can hand to a child. It comes from making real decisions and seeing what happens, ideally where mistakes cost nothing.

quotes.hook: Are you doing too much for your child?
quotes.quote: No one can be free unless he is independent.
quotes.author: Maria Montessori
quotes.source: Maria Montessori, The Montessori Method (1912), chapter V, translated by Anne E. George.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #39863) on 16 November 2026. The sentence continues after a colon in the original.
quotes.takeaway: Independence is built one small responsibility at a time.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Montessori saw independence as the first goal of education. At home it can start small: one job, one decision, one thing a child manages alone.

quotes.hook: How do you raise a kind child?
quotes.quote: No one is useless in this world who lightens the burden of it for any one else.
quotes.author: Charles Dickens
quotes.source: Charles Dickens, Our Mutual Friend (1865), Book the Third, chapter 9. Spoken by John Rokesmith.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #883) on 16 November 2026. In the novel the line is interrupted by "retorted the Secretary"; the narration is omitted.
quotes.takeaway: Kindness and giving are skills children can practise.
quotes.cta: Try the giving activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: A line from Dickens that children understand straight away: helping someone matters. Giving time, a toy or a little money is a habit that can start young.
